fuentes: USDA FSIS: Stuffing and Food Safety / Turkey Basics: Stuffing (center of stuffing must reach 165 °F, use a food thermometer; do not remove stuffing before 165 °F, keep cooking the turkey until it gets there; for optimum safety and uniform doneness, cook stuffing outside the bird)

frases.texto: You stuffed the turkey, and the turkey's done. The stuffing might not be.
frases.estilo: Dry, direct, with a half smile.

frases.texto: The USDA says stuffing cooked inside the bird has to reach one hundred sixty-five degrees at the center.
The thigh can read done while the middle of the stuffing is still behind.
frases.estilo: Matter of fact, a little surprised.

frases.texto: So stick a food thermometer right into the center of the stuffing.
Don't pull it out before it hits one sixty-five. Keep cooking the turkey until it gets there.
Heads up: for the safest, most even result, the USDA says to bake stuffing in a separate dish.
Stuffing or dressing? What do you call it?
Save this, then send it to the friend who stuffs the bird and trusts the timer.
